# Staging hosting and deployment decision

**Decision date:** 2026-08-09

**Status:** RECOMMENDED, NOT PROVISIONED
**Cost generated by this decision:** EUR 0

This document selects a practical public staging shape for SocialOS. It does not authorize account creation, billing, DNS changes, secret creation, provisioning, deployment, Meta configuration, or production traffic. Prices and limits are a snapshot from official provider documentation on the decision date and must be rechecked immediately before purchase.

## Requirements

The staging environment must run the existing production images for Next.js, FastAPI and Celery, plus PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible media storage. It needs persistent data, a stable HTTPS origin, a worker that does not sleep, private database/broker networking, isolated migrations, structured logs, recoverable backups and a path to later separation of services.

The runtime contract already merged in PR #85 supplies environment validation, immutable-image Compose, a separate migration job, readiness checks, request correlation and S3-compatible media. No additional application code is required to select a provider.

## Pricing snapshot and official sources

- [Oracle Always Free documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/FreeTier/freetier_topic-Always_Free_Resources.htm): up to 2 OCPUs/12 GB A1 memory, 200 GB combined block volume, five volume backups and 20 GB object storage for eligible Always Free accounts. Oracle documents possible `out of host capacity` errors and normally requires a card and phone during signup.
- [Hetzner June 2026 prices](https://docs.hetzner.com/general/infrastructure-and-availability/price-adjustment/): Germany/Finland CX23 is EUR 5.49/month after the adjustment, excluding VAT and IPv4. Recheck final checkout price and hardware availability.
- [Railway pricing](https://railway.com/pricing): Hobby has a USD 5 minimum with USD 5 usage included; memory is USD 0.00000386/GB-second, CPU USD 0.00000772/vCPU-second, volume USD 0.00000006/GB-second and service egress USD 0.05/GB. A continuously running multi-service stack cannot safely be budgeted at only USD 5.
- [Railway volume backups](https://docs.railway.com/volumes/backups): daily backups retain 6 days, weekly 1 month and monthly 3 months; restore creates a staged replacement volume.
- [Render free limitations](https://render.com/docs/free): free web services share 750 hours and spin down; free Postgres is 1 GB, expires after 30 days and has no backups; free Key Value is memory-only. [Background workers](https://render.com/docs/service-types) are a separate persistent service type and do not have a free instance type.
- [Fly.io pricing](https://fly.io/docs/about/pricing/): running shared Machines start at USD 2.02/month for 256 MB and USD 5.92/month for 1 GB, plus volumes and managed data services. [The current trial](https://fly.io/docs/about/free-trial/) ends after 2 VM hours or 7 days.
- [Google Cloud Free Tier](https://docs.cloud.google.com/free/docs/free-cloud-features): one US-region e2-micro, 30 GB-month standard disk and 1 GB outbound transfer per month. This is insufficient headroom for the complete SocialOS stack.
- [Neon pricing](https://neon.com/pricing): Free has 0.5 GB storage, 100 CU-hours monthly per project and a 6-hour time-travel/restore window; Launch lists a typical intermittent 1 GB workload at USD 15/month.
- [Upstash Redis pricing](https://upstash.com/pricing/redis): Free has 256 MB, 10 GB bandwidth and 500K commands/month. Production HA/SLA features are paid.
- [Cloudflare R2 pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/): Standard includes 10 GB-month, 1M Class A and 10M Class B operations monthly at no charge, with free egress. Beyond free usage it is USD 0.015/GB-month plus operations.
- [Cloudflare R2 public delivery](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/platform/limits/): `r2.dev` is development-only and rate-limited; stable public media should use a custom domain. [Presigned PUT URLs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/presigned-urls/) use the S3 API domain, while reads can use the custom media domain.
- [Vercel pricing](https://vercel.com/pricing): Hobby is USD 0 and Pro is USD 20/month, but neither replaces the persistent FastAPI/Celery/PostgreSQL/Redis runtime.

## Candidate architectures

### Option A — Zero-cost experiment

- One Oracle Ampere A1 Always Free VM: Caddy, web, API, worker, PostgreSQL and Redis through Docker Compose.
- OCI Object Storage through the S3-compatible adapter, or R2 after separate approval.
- Persistent block volume with encrypted database dumps and a restore drill.
- Estimated infrastructure cost: **EUR 0 when every resource remains Always Free**; domain is extra.
- Trade-offs: signup generally requires a card, eligible capacity can be unavailable, operations and database recovery are self-managed, and free resources do not constitute a production SLA.

This is acceptable for a disposable technical experiment, not the preferred shared staging environment when reliability matters.

### Option B — Cheapest practical staging (selected)

- One Hetzner CX23-class VM in Germany or Finland.
- Docker Compose runs Caddy, Next.js, FastAPI, Celery, PostgreSQL and Redis on a private Docker network.
- Cloudflare R2 Standard stores public media through the existing S3 adapter.
- Nightly encrypted `pg_dump` leaves the VM; provider snapshot/backup strategy is verified and restore-tested before external testers are invited.
- Estimated baseline: **EUR 5.49/month excluding VAT, IPv4, domain and overages**, plus R2 at EUR 0 while inside its free limits. Final checkout price is TBD and requires explicit approval.

This preserves the current Docker architecture, keeps the worker alive, minimizes vendor-specific code and can later split PostgreSQL/Redis into managed services.

### Option C — Simplest managed operations

- Railway services for web, API, worker, migration job, PostgreSQL and Redis; Railway object storage or Cloudflare R2.
- Railway service domain initially; custom domain before stable Meta OAuth.
- Built-in deploy logs, private networking, health checks, rollbacks and volume backups.
- Estimated low-traffic staging: **USD 20–40/month** as a planning range, not a quote. The hard minimum is USD 5, but continuous memory/CPU and data services are metered. A provider calculator and a hard usage alert are mandatory before authorization.

This has the least operational burden but a higher and variable bill and greater PaaS coupling.

## Selected staging architecture

```text
Internet
  |
  | HTTPS
  v
staging.<confirmed-domain>  -> Caddy on one Hetzner VM
  |-- /api/*                -> FastAPI container
  |-- all other paths       -> Next.js container
  |
  +-- private Docker network
        |-- Celery worker
        |-- PostgreSQL volume
        `-- Redis AOF volume

Browser -- presigned PUT --> Cloudflare R2 S3 endpoint
Browser <-- public media --- media.staging.<confirmed-domain>
```

Use a single application origin for staging: `https://staging.<confirmed-domain>`. The reverse proxy sends `/api/*` to FastAPI and everything else to Next.js. This removes cross-origin application calls, simplifies cookies and CSP, and reduces CORS to the one explicit origin. Media remains on `https://media.staging.<confirmed-domain>` because browser uploads use presigned S3 URLs and published media must be publicly retrievable.

Do not use `socialos.ai` or any canonical hostname until ownership is confirmed. Do not use a Quick Tunnel as the staging identity.

## Environment and secrets

Create secrets only after provider approval. They must live in a root-owned environment file outside Git and be injected into Compose, or in the selected provider's secret manager. Never bake them into images or expose them to Next.js public variables.

Server-only values include `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `META_APP_SECRET`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` and S3 endpoint/bucket configuration. `META_APP_ID`, `META_LOGIN_CONFIG_ID` and the Clerk publishable key are identifiers/public configuration but should still be managed centrally. Generate separate staging credentials; never copy production values.

Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values may reach the browser. The web container receives `API_INTERNAL_URL=http://api:8000/api/v1`; browsers use the same public origin through `/api`.

## Database, media backups and recovery

Initial targets are **RECOMMENDED/TBD until a restore exercise succeeds**:

- PostgreSQL RPO: 24 hours for supervised staging; target 1 hour once real beta data matters.
- PostgreSQL RTO: 4 hours for supervised staging.
- Nightly encrypted logical dump to storage outside the VM; retain 7 daily and 4 weekly copies.
- Weekly provider disk snapshot when its exact price and retention are approved.
- Test restoration into an isolated database before calling backups active.
- Redis is a broker/cache, not the source of truth. Enable AOF for graceful restart, but rebuild queues from publication state when necessary.
- R2 keeps original objects. Enable an explicit retention/versioning or backup policy only after checking its cost; lifecycle rules must never delete referenced media accidentally.

No backup is currently active merely because this plan exists.

## Deployment sequence after explicit authorization

1. Recheck provider prices, VAT, IPv4, domain availability and spending cap.
2. Obtain explicit approval for the exact maximum monthly cost.
3. Provision one VM, firewall and persistent disk; expose only 80/443 and restricted administration access.
4. Confirm or register a domain separately, then configure `staging` and `media.staging` DNS records.
5. Create R2 bucket/CORS/API credentials and secrets without printing values.
6. Build immutable images from a green Git SHA and transfer/pull those exact digests.
7. Run the one-shot Alembic migration job.
8. Start API, worker and web; require healthy live/ready checks before routing traffic.
9. Verify PostgreSQL/Redis are unreachable publicly, public media works and logs correlate request IDs.
10. Run tenant isolation, upload, publication, retry/cancel and backup/restore smoke tests.
11. Invite supervised testers only after the acceptance checklist passes.

Rollback uses the prior immutable API/web image digests. Do not blindly downgrade a migrated schema. Stop routing, preserve database/log evidence, and restore data only through a rehearsed recovery procedure.

## Future Meta staging transition

Meta is not changed by this decision. After staging exists:

1. verify `https://staging.<confirmed-domain>/health` and the frontend callback route;
2. add `https://staging.<confirmed-domain>/integrations/meta/callback` as an allowed Redirect URI in Meta for Developers;
3. set `WEB_BASE_URL` and `META_REDIRECT_URI` to that exact stable HTTPS value;
4. perform one supervised OAuth connection and validate scopes/account selection;
5. perform an explicitly authorized test publication and reconcile its final state;
6. retain the temporary Quick Tunnel URI only during a short transition, then remove it after the stable callback is proven.

The OAuth callback, app secret, tokens and Configuration ID must never appear in logs or frontend state.

## Manual decisions and cost guard

Before any deployment the founder must approve:

- provider and region;
- final checkout amount including VAT/IPv4;
- domain ownership or purchase;
- monthly hard cap and alerts;
- backup destination and retention;
- staging access policy;
- creation of provider, R2 and DNS resources;
- the later Meta Redirect URI change.

No VM, database, Redis instance, bucket, project, domain, DNS record, billing account, trial or card was created or changed while producing this decision.

## Production later

Staging deliberately starts consolidated. Production should separate managed PostgreSQL with point-in-time recovery, durable Redis, multiple API/worker instances, private networking, centralized secret management and off-host observability only after load, compliance needs and revenue justify the cost. AWS/ECS or another managed platform can then consume the same images and ports without changing domain logic.

**Staging provider:** Hetzner Cloud + Cloudflare R2 — RECOMMENDED

**Staging:** NOT_DEPLOYED

**Production:** NOT_DEPLOYED
